text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended marginally firmer in thin trading. Spot October accounted for the bulk of the turnover but much of this came in the form of October/March spread trading, with little interest seen in the second-month December contract. October ended 20 cents higher at $327.90. December added $1.20 to close at $324.00 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed higher after the benchmark October contract failed to erode support and attracted short-covering and fund buying. October closed 10 points higher at 11.68 cents/lb, while March added 10 points to close at 11.88 cents/lb. It is expected that Friday's commitment of traders report will show that speculators are holding more than 50 per cent of net long positions. FUNDAMENTALS

THAILAND ** - It is generally expected that Thai sugar production in 1997/98 (November/October) will be lower than last year, due to lack of rain. Now trade sources said that the total in 1997/98 could be 5.03 million tonnes, tel quel, down from 5.80 million tonnes in 1996/97 and 6.03 million tonnes in 1995/96. Molasses production in 1997/98 is forecast to reach 2.39 million tonnes, down from 2.59 million tonnes produced the previous year and 2.85 million tonnes produced in 1995/96.

CHINA ** - Sugar imports picked up in June 1997 with the total reaching 150,666 tonnes, raw value, up from 76,251 tonnes in May, but still down on the 191,974 tonnes imported in June 1996. The June shipments brought cumulative imports so far in 1996/97 (September/June) up to 783,930 tonnes, down from 1.674 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.944 million tonnes compared to 2.907 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Australia with 299,770 tonnes raws against 351,995 tonnes, Cuba with 260,897 tonnes compared to 269,639 tonnes and Thailand with 152,163 tonnes against 559,517 tonnes. The largest white sugar supplier in September/June 1996/97 continued to be South Korea with 32,298 tonnes against 26,557 tonnes.

Sugar exports in June 1997 amounted to 31,250 tonnes, down from 39,382 tonnes in June 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/June 1996/97 up to 286,082 tonnes compared to 746,119 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 830,203 tonnes compared to 540,004 tonnes in 1995/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Pakistan with 111,624 tonnes whites against nil, Saudi Arabia with 79,080 tonnes, down from 232,000 tonnes and Hong Kong with 30,330 tonnes against 82,403 tonnes.

GERMANY ** - Sugar production in June 1997 amounted to 11,015 tonnes, raw avlue, which brought cumulative production in the first three quarters of 1996/97 up to 4.561 million tonnes against 4.151 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total production in 1995/96 amounted to 4.158 million tonnes against 3.991 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Sugar consumption jumped to 284,463 tonnes in June, up from 257,510 tonnes the same month in 1996. This brought total consumption in 1996/97 (October/June) up to 2.245 million tonnes against 2.228 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total consumption in 1995/96 was 3.076 million tonnes against 2.995 million tonnes in 1994/95.

GREECE ** - The latest beet test result of July 21 shows that the beet crop is still on course for recovery after last year's dismal results. Beet weight per ha amounted to 46.52 tonnes compared to 44.44 tonnes in 1996, but down on the 55.88 tonnes in 1995. Sugar content reached 13.35 per cent against 13.05 per cent in 1996 and 12.60 per cent in 1995. This resulted in a sugar weight per ha of 6.20 tonnes, white value, compared to 5.77 tonnes in 1996 and 7.05 tonnes in 1995. Given the better results and the larger area sown to beet sugar production can be expected to rise to 365,000 tonnes, white value, compared to 265,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
